answer: Bond curve per operator: to register, an agent locks POA in a bond whose price doubles for every identity already tied to the same funding harbor, so the operator pays and fake N costs twice fake N-1. Links are found by tracing deposits, and each bond carries a cipher commitment to its funder that auditors can open. Failure case: an attacker who launders funds through a willow of fresh wallets still pays, because bonds stay locked for 30 epochs and unbonding early forfeits half.
